summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet stated that the Cambodian government will protect and support internally displaced people (IDPs) affected by the conflict with Thailand. He noted that the national budget and help from development partners would be used to rebuild infrastructure damaged during the fighting.
title: PM Hun Manet Pledges Support for Citizens Displaced by Border Conflict

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet emphasized that Cambodia has not ceded any land to Thailand. He stated that the government chose a peaceful path through international law and diplomatic mechanisms rather than violence to ensure a lasting solution. He rejected rumors that the ceasefire involved giving up territory, affirming that surveying and border management work continues under international law.
title: Hun Manet: Cambodia Has Not Given Up Sovereignty Claims

summary: The Ministry of Interior reported that between Jan 31 and Feb 1, 753 more displaced civilians returned to their homes. Since the Dec 27, 2025 ceasefire, about 83% of the 640,000 displaced persons have returned, but 111,509 people remain in camps. The ministry noted that while no new fighting has occurred, they remain vigilant regarding Thai military activities and the impact on civilians.
title: Ministry of Interior: 753 more displaced persons return home

summary: Cambodia's State Secretariat of Border Affairs issued a formal protest on Jan 31, 2026, alleging that Thai military units are clearing and destroying homes of Cambodian citizens in border areas. The secretariat proposed a timeline of Feb 9–13 for Joint Survey Teams to meet and resume placing temporary markers near pillars 42–47 and 52–59, stating that Thailand has not yet responded to a previous request from mid-January.
title: Cambodia presses Thailand to act on stalled border demarcation, protests military actions

summary: Senate First Vice President Ouch Borith informed the Parliamentary Assembly of La Francophonie (APF) that the border situation has 'deteriorated significantly.' He accused Thai troops of not respecting the December 27 ceasefire by invading Cambodian territory and installing wire fences and containers to block Cambodian civilians from their homes.
title: Ouch Borith highlights deteriorating border situation at APF meeting

summary: At a UN Security Council meeting in New York on Friday (Jan 30), Cambodian Ambassador Keo Chhea and Thai representative Cherdchai Chaivaivid exchanged legal arguments. Cambodia accused Thailand of disregarding the 1907 Franco-Siamese Treaty and 'uti possidetis juris' (maintaining borders as they were at independence/treaty signing). Thailand responded by rejecting 'selective' application of international law and emphasized bilateral mechanisms like the JBC. This follows two major military clashes in July and December 2025.
title: Cambodia and Thailand spar again on the global stage over border dispute

summary: Military representatives from Cambodia’s 4th Military Region and Thailand’s 2nd Army Region met at the Choam-Sa Ngam international gate in Oddar Meanchey. Despite the presence of ASEAN Observer Teams (AOT), the two sides could not reach a 'common middle point' and agreed to return to their respective headquarters to continue exchanging documents.
title: Regional Border Committee (RBC) secretariat groups meet under AOT observation

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet has announced a three-point recovery plan for over 500,000 citizens displaced by the border conflict. While 540,000 have returned home, over 111,000 remain in camps, primarily because Thai forces are allegedly occupying six villages in Banteay Meanchey province and other areas in Preah Vihear and Oddar Meanchey, preventing safe return. The government is assessing damage to schools and infrastructure for reconstruction.
title: Govt prepares salve after border displacement salvo

summary: Government spokesperson Pen Bona stated that Cambodia has sent multiple formal requests (Note Verbales) to Thailand to resume joint border surveys between February 9-13. The Cambodian side 'strongly protests' against Thai military units clearing and destroying homes and property of Cambodian citizens and preventing them from returning to their residences, which violates the December ceasefire agreement.
title: Cambodia urges Thailand to respect and implement point 3 of joint declaration of December 27, 2025 without delay

summary: In an official government statement, Cambodia issued a sharp rebuke against Thailand, alleging military occupation of Cambodian soil despite the ceasefire. The report claims Thai troops are blocking civilians from their homes and damaging heritage sites, including a statue of Vishnu. Cambodia called on the international community to help restore stability based on the 1904 and 1907 treaties.
title: Cambodia Accuses Thailand of Violations in Border Dispute

summary: Professor Chheang Ra, Minister of Health, visited Preah Vihear to support medical staff and displaced persons. He claimed that approximately 70 health facilities including provincial and referral hospitals along the border were 'damaged or destroyed' during two separate Thai military incursions. He also distributed medical kits donated by UNFPA to help war refugees.
title: Health Minister visits Preah Vihear health centers affected by Cambodia-Thailand border conflict

summary: Wing Bank announced its second round of loan relief, writing off $150,000 in debt for families affected by the fighting in Oddar Meanchey, Banteay Meanchey, and Preah Vihear provinces. Some families saw 75% reductions, while others had full balances cleared. This brings the bank's total border relief to $200,000 since September last year.
title: Wing Bank Writes Off Additional USD 150,000 in Loans for Border-Affected Families

summary: Cambodia is scheduled to host a trilateral summit with the top leaders of Vietnam and Laos on February 6-7, 2026. While the official agenda focuses on traditional ties, analysts believe the meeting is a signal of regional solidarity intended to strengthen Cambodia's position amidst the current border dispute and security threats from Thailand.
title: Cambodia to Host Vietnam-Laos Leaders as Analyst Sees Potential Impact on Thailand Tensions

summary: Senate First Vice-President Ouch Borith warned an international parliamentary assembly in Montenegro that the border situation with Thailand is deteriorating. He accused Thai forces of violating the December 27 ceasefire by moving into Cambodian territory and erecting barriers like barbed wire and shipping containers. He specifically mentioned damage to the Preah Vihear Temple, a UNESCO site, calling it an assault on national identity.
title: Cambodia raises alarm over 'escalating' border row

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFAIC) lodged a formal protest against an 'unauthorised field visit' by Thai military intelligence and foreign attaches to two hotels in O Smach. Cambodia claims the area is sovereign territory currently 'occupied by force' by Thai troops since the December 2025 offensive. Thailand maintains the sites were being used as hubs for online scam operations.
title: Cambodia Slams Thai Military-Led “Field Visit” to Hotels in Occupied O Smach District

summary: Lt. Gen. Meung Ponlok, Director General of Logistics and Finance at the Ministry of National Defence, donated ambulances, medical beds, and financial aid to troops at the Thailand border. He specifically visited soldiers receiving treatment for injuries sustained during the border conflict at Military Hospital Region 5 (P-2) in Battambang.
title: General Meung Ponlok delivers ambulances to Border Guard Unit 501 and medical supplies to Military Hospital Region 5

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs lodged a formal protest against Thailand regarding an unauthorized field visit on Feb 2, 2026. The visit, led by the Thai Army's Chief of Intelligence and involving foreign military attachés, took place at two hotels in O Smach District, Oddar Meanchey. Cambodia claims these hotels are 397 meters inside Cambodian territory and are currently being occupied by force following the Thai military offensive in December 2025.
title: Cambodia protests against unauthorized field visit led by Chief of Intelligence of Thai Army in Cambodian Territory

summary: Data from the Thai Foreign Trade Department shows that border trade with Cambodia fell by 47.3% in 2025 due to armed clashes and subsequent border closures. The outlook for 2026 remains bleak as ongoing tensions prevent the reopening of key trade gates, causing significant economic loss for local communities on both sides.
title: Thai border trade drops due to conflict with Cambodia and civil war in Myanmar

summary: Military commanders from Cambodia's Military Region 3 and Thailand's Chanthaburi–Trat Border Defence Command met at the Cham Yeam-Hat Lek border crossing. The meeting was observed by the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT). While both sides reaffirmed their commitment to reducing tensions and returning to normalcy after the 2025 clashes, they failed to reach a consensus on specific points and agreed to continue document exchanges.
title: Cambodia–Thailand RBC holds special meeting in Koh Kong under AOT

summary: PM Hun Manet briefed the Supreme Consultation and Recommendation Council on short, medium, and long-term solutions for the border crisis. He asserted that while Cambodia seeks peaceful resolution through ASEAN and international legal channels, it will not cede territory. The government maintains that 'de facto occupation' by Thai forces does not constitute legal ownership under international law.
title: Cambodia Deploys Multiple Mechanisms to Solve Border Dispute with Thailand

summary: Government spokesperson Pen Bona detailed a formal protest against an unauthorized visit by Thai military intelligence and foreign attachés to two hotels in O Smach, Oddar Meanchey. The hotels are located 397 meters from the border and were allegedly occupied by Thai forces during the December offensive. Cambodia labels this an 'illegitimate exercise of sovereignty.' The briefing also mentions damage to the Ta Krabei Temple due to Thai military actions.
title: Press Briefing by H.E. Pen Bona, Royal Government Spokesperson: Update on the Development of the Situation between Cambodia and Thailand, 04 February 2026

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet has formally requested French President Emmanuel Macron to provide historical documents and technical expertise to help settle the border dispute. Cambodia is seeking 1907-era maps and French advisory support to clarify the boundary line, following two armed clashes last year. The request follows France's earlier indication that it was ready to assist with historical records.
title: Cambodia Requests French Technical Support for Thai Border Mapping

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet has formally requested historical border maps and technical documents from French President Emmanuel Macron. The request aims to bolster Cambodia's legal position regarding the 1907 Franco-Siamese Treaty maps. This move comes after two major military clashes in 2025, with Cambodia pushing for a solution based on international law and historical evidence to prevent further bloodshed.
title: Cambodia Seeks French Historical Records to Resolve Thai Border Dispute

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFAIC) issued a protest note after Thai forces placed three shipping containers in An Seh village, Preah Vihear province, on February 3. Cambodia claims this move obstructs the An Seh International Border Checkpoint and violates the existing border agreements. This follows a pattern of 'creeping' infrastructure placement reported by local border authorities.
title: Cambodia Lodges Another Protest against Thai Military Actions in An Seh Area

source: Press OCM (Press and Quick Reaction Unit)
summary: Lt. Gen. Mali Socheata, spokesperson for the Ministry of National Defense, denied Thai media reports claiming Cambodia fired a 40mm grenade near a Thai military base. She called it 'fabricated news' intended to mislead the public and increase border tension. Military Region 4 confirmed through contact with Thailand's 2nd Army Area that no such incident occurred. Cambodia reaffirmed its commitment to the December 27, 2025, GBC ceasefire agreement.
title: Ministry of National Defense completely rejects fake news from Thai media about 40mm grenade landing near Phlan Hin Pet Kon base

summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFAIC) formally protested against Thai armed forces for placing three shipping containers in the An Seh area of Preah Vihear province on February 3. Cambodia claims this obstructs access to the international border gate and violates the ceasefire agreement from December 27, 2025. The move is viewed by Phnom Penh as an attempt to consolidate illegal occupation of Cambodian territory.
title: Cambodia lodges another protest against Thai military actions in An Seh area

summary: Keo Remy, President of the Cambodian Human Rights Committee, stated that the Thai military's occupation of Cambodian territory is legally unacceptable. He framed the situation as an act of aggression that violates international norms, reflecting the government's stance that Thai forces remain in areas they should have vacated under previous agreements.
title: Keo Remy: Territorial aggression by Thai military to occupy is illegal

summary: Authorities in Oddar Meanchey province report that Thai forces advanced 420 meters into Cambodian territory at the O'Smach International Border Checkpoint. Officials claim Thai troops occupied government buildings (Customs, Immigration) and raised the Thai flag near Border Marker No. 15. The deputy governor stated that Thai forces have installed concrete drainage boxes and laid barbed wire, creating fear among local residents and traders at the now-closed border market.
title: Thai Troops Illegally Occupy 420 Metres inside O’Smach International Border Area Despite Agreed Boundary Marker

summary: Senior Minister Keo Remy briefed US District Judge John C. Coughenour on the border conflict, alleging that Thai forces used F-16 and Gripen jets to penetrate 90km into Cambodia. He claimed the attacks targeted UNESCO sites and used cluster munitions. According to the CHRC, the judge expressed support for Cambodia's restraint and disappointment over the Thai military's use of heavy weaponry against civilians.
title: Senior Minister Keo Remy Meets Senior US Judge to Discuss Border Dispute, Human Rights

summary: Keo Remy, Chairman of the Cambodian Human Rights Committee, met with a senior US judge to report human rights violations resulting from the border conflict. He alleged that Thai forces used heavy weaponry that impacted areas up to 90km inside Cambodian territory. The briefing also touched upon the 1907 Franco-Siamese Treaty and French willingness to provide historical maps to support Cambodia's territorial claims.
title: Cambodian Human Rights Chief Tells US Senior Judge: Thailand Used Heavy Weapons 90km Deep into Cambodia

summary: The Cambodian National Force Party (NFP) has submitted a petition to King Norodom Sihamoni, urging him to encourage the government to file a case against Thailand at the International Court of Justice (ICJ). The party claims that Thailand is occupying 45 locations along the border, including parts of Koh Kut. The petition follows reports that over 90,000 Cambodian civilians remain displaced in camps due to the 2025 conflict.
title: National Force Party seeks the King to help push the government to use international law to reclaim Cambodian land from invading Thailand

summary: Lieutenant General Maly Socheata, spokeswoman for the Ministry of National Defence, categorically denied reports from Thai media claiming Cambodia fired 40mm grenades near the Phlan Hin Pet Kon military base on February 5. The ministry labeled the reports 'fabricated' and 'intended to mislead public opinion.' Military coordination teams from both sides reportedly contacted each other and confirmed no such incident took place.
title: Cambodian Defence Ministry rejects Thai media reports alleging grenade fire near border base

summary: Oddar Meanchey provincial authorities reported that the Ou Chik Bridge on National Road 68 was completely destroyed by three MK82 bombs dropped by Thai F-16 aircraft in late December. While the incident happened previously, officials highlight today that the damage continues to affect the livelihoods of over 100,000 people (24,433 families) in Chong Kal and Samraong districts. Officials emphasize that the bridge is 60km away from the border, citing it as clear evidence of an 'invasion' rather than a mere border dispute.
title: After Thai military invasion, Ou Chik Bridge cut off, affecting over 100,000 people in Oddar Meanchey and Siem Reap

summary: Heng Ratana, Director General of the Cambodian Mine Action Centre (CMAC), stated that remains of cluster bombs, chemical munitions, and aerial bombs found in civilian areas serve as proof of Thai military aggression. He claimed these weapons impacted Cambodian territorial integrity and civilian safety during recent clashes. The report includes visuals of the munitions found in residential sites.
title: Heavy bomb remains in residential areas and public places are undeniable evidence of Thai military aggression on Cambodian territory

summary: The Deputy Governor of Oddar Meanchey reported that Thai forces have encroached 420 meters into Cambodian territory at the O’Smach International Border Checkpoint. The official noted significant damage to schools, pagodas, and homes due to previous shelling. Thai troops have blocked Cambodian authorities from accessing administrative buildings at the gate.
title: Thai Troops' 420-Metre Encroachment at O'Smach Border Checkpoint Ignores International Law, Says Deputy Governor

summary: Residents of border villages like Chouk Chey describe losing their homes and farms as Thai forces moved the boundary line following clashes in 2025. Over 1,200 families remain in displacement shelters. While Thailand claims it is reclaiming its own land, Cambodian villagers report their houses were bulldozed after the December ceasefire.
title: A tale of two villages: Cambodians lament Thailand's border gains

summary: Thai troops reportedly deployed seven shipping containers and reinforced barbed wire barricades in the Thmar Da area of Pursat province early Saturday morning. A high-ranking official stated the movement was accompanied by armored vehicles and a significant military presence. Cambodia has condemned the act as an illegal violation of the ceasefire and national sovereignty.
title: Breaking News: Thai Troops Block Road with Shipping Containers in Thmar Da Area, Pursat

summary: PM Hun Manet sent a letter to French President Emmanuel Macron thanking him for France's readiness to provide historical maps and technical documents regarding the 1904 and 1907 treaties. Cambodia hopes these colonial-era records will serve as definitive legal evidence to settle the current border dispute with Thailand without the use of force.
title: Border cannot be invaded by force: French documents expected to end border dispute legally for the 3rd time

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a strong protest against Thai armed forces for placing containers to block road access and starting road construction in Oddar Meanchey and Pursat provinces. Cambodia claims these areas are well within its territory according to the 1904 and 1907 treaties and that these actions breach the de-escalation measures agreed upon in December 2025.
title: Cambodia Protests against Thai Military's Activities in Occupied Cambodian Territory

summary: According to the Deputy Governor of Oddar Meanchey, Thai military forces have encroached 400 meters into Cambodian territory near the O'Smach International Border Gate. The incursions, involving the placement of large concrete blocks and barbed wire, occurred just one day after a ceasefire was renewed. Local authorities claim government offices and private resorts in the area are now surrounded by Thai troops.
title: Thai military places concrete culverts and barbed wire 400m inside Cambodia near O'Smach

summary: Cambodia has issued a strong protest against ongoing activities by the Thai military in disputed zones. The government claims Thai troops are still occupying areas in Oddar Meanchey and Pursat despite the ceasefire. Cambodia insists on resolving these issues through peaceful means and international law but remains resolute against territorial violations.
title: Cambodia protests against the actions of Thai armed forces in occupying Cambodian territory

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Interior reported that as of February 8, 2026, a total of 86,447 displaced civilians remain in temporary camps due to the border conflict. This group includes 45,376 women and 28,012 children. The report highlights the ongoing humanitarian impact on civilian areas along the frontier following the hostilities that peaked in December 2025.
title: Ministry of Interior: 86,447 displaced people still living in camps

summary: The Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts rejected claims by Thai Culture Minister Sabida Thaiseth that the Ta Krabey and Ta Mone temple complexes fall under Thai sovereignty. The ministry reaffirmed that these sites are entirely within Cambodia according to international legal foundations and called on Thailand to cease unilateral restoration work or military occupation of cultural heritage sites.
title: Cambodian Culture Ministry Firmly Rejects Thai Minister's Claim over Ta Krabey and Ta Mone Temples

summary: During a visit to displacement camps for civilians fleeing the border conflict, the EU Ambassador to Cambodia expressed solidarity and promised continued support. The visit highlights the ongoing humanitarian crisis, with thousands of families living in temporary shelters in pagodas and schools across Banteay Meanchey and Oddar Meanchey provinces. The government is reportedly planning to transition these camps into more permanent 'temporary shelters' as many remain unable to return home due to Thai troop presence.
title: EU Ambassador Pledges Continued Aid to Displaced Families in Banteay Meanchey

summary: Cambodian security officials have officially rejected reports from Thai media outlets that claimed Phnom Penh is building up its military and acquiring advanced anti-aircraft weapons. The Cambodian side called these reports 'unfounded' and 'misleading,' stating that they remain committed to the December 27, 2025 ceasefire agreement and peaceful dialogue via the General Border Committee (GBC).
title: Security officials dismiss Thai media’s ‘unfounded and misleading’ claims of military escalation

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFAIC) issued a formal protest against the Thai military's installation of shipping containers and roadblocks in Oddar Meanchey and Pursat provinces. Cambodia claims these barriers are placed within its sovereign territory and violate the de-escalation measures agreed upon in the December 27, 2025 ceasefire. While Thailand claims these are temporary security measures to prevent vandalism, Phnom Penh views them as an attempt to create 'new realities on the ground.'
title: Government protests Thai military roadblocks along border

summary: The O'Smach International Border Checkpoint, once a bustling trade hub, has seen its market of 700 shops abandoned. Local residents report that Thai troops have advanced 420 meters past the mutually recognized Border Marker 15, occupying government buildings and raising Thai flags on the Cambodian side. This military presence, combined with damage from previous artillery shelling, has prevented traders and civilians from returning to their homes despite the official ceasefire.
title: Thai army presence turns O’Smach market into ghost town

summary: Local officials in Pursat province report that Thai troops have reinforced barricades with seven shipping containers and armored vehicles in the Thmar Da area. Governor Khoy Rida stated that the encroachment affects four specific locations and has displaced over 80 families. The report highlights a verbal confrontation between Thai forces and Chinese business owners in the area, witnessed by journalists. Cambodia describes the move as an 'illegal occupation' following military assaults in late 2025.
title: Cambodia cries foul over Thai occupation of Thmar Da

summary: According to the Ministry of Interior, out of more than 640,000 people displaced by the border conflict since December, about 86,271 civilians remain unable to return to their homes. While 87% have returned, many are still blocked from their properties in areas now occupied or restricted by Thai forces, particularly in Oddar Meanchey and Pursat provinces.
title: Over 86,000 displaced people still unable to return home

summary: Cambodian security officials in Preah Vihear province have rejected Thai media reports of a military build-up and a possible 'third round' of fighting. Officials labeled these reports as 'unfounded and misleading' attempts to create fear after the Thai elections. Cambodia reaffirmed its commitment to the December 27 ceasefire and called on the international community to support a peaceful resolution.
title: Cambodia dismisses Thai claims of 'third round' of fighting

summary: During a meeting with the Cambodian Human Rights Committee, Japanese Ambassador Ueno Atsushi promised to report the border situation to Tokyo. Cambodian officials informed him that 90,000 displaced people cannot return home safely due to Thai military's illegal occupation and the use of barbed wire and containers at the border. Cambodia accused Thailand of using F-16 and Gripen jets in previous attacks.
title: Japanese Ambassador to Cambodia says he will inform his government of the Cambodia-Thailand border issue

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet stated that the Cambodia-Thailand border is an international boundary protected by the UN Charter. He emphasized that Cambodia will not recognize any changes to border lines or illegal occupation achieved through force. He also noted a letter sent to French President Macron requesting historical and technical documents (colonial maps) to help resolve the boundary dispute through the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC).
title: PM Hun Manet: Royal Government Committed to Protecting Territorial Integrity Based on International Law, Absolutely Rejects Territorial Control by Force

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet stated that the Cambodia-Thailand border is an international boundary protected by the UN Charter. He emphasized that the government will use all legal means to protect sovereignty and will never recognize border changes made through force. He noted that while there are many differing views, the government is working constantly to resolve the issue, even if not always shown publicly.
title: Cambodian PM declares absolute non-recognition of border changes via Thai military force

summary: In an emotional address to 'Grade A' students, PM Hun Manet acknowledged the psychological impact of the border conflict on Cambodians. He urged the nation to stay strong and united, stating that while the conflict is 'painful,' it must be used as motivation to strengthen the nation's capacity. He noted that the border has unfortunately turned back into a battlefield recently but expressed hope for a return to development.
title: PM Hun Manet’s Political Message: 'We cannot let the pain of territorial disputes with Thailand knock us down; we must turn pain into strength'

summary: During a speech on February 10, PM Hun Manet reaffirmed Cambodia's commitment to the UN Charter regarding border disputes. He revealed that on February 4, he sent a letter to French President Emmanuel Macron requesting technical expertise and historical colonial-era documents to aid in accurate border demarcation. He insisted on using the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) to resolve current tensions peacefully.
title: PM: Cambodia will defend its territory under International Law, rejects border seizure by force

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts has officially rejected claims made by Thailand's Culture Minister regarding sovereignty over the Ta Krabei and Ta Moan temple complexes. Cambodia asserts these sites fall under its jurisdiction based on colonial-era treaties and warns that any 'restoration' by Thailand without consent violates the 2000 MOU. The ministry signaled it is ready to take the matter to the International Court of Justice (ICJ).
title: Cambodia baulks at Thai claims over Ta Krabei and Ta Moan

summary: The Royal Thai Navy arrested 10 Cambodian nationals (3 men, 4 women, and 3 children) on February 8 in Chanthaburi Province. The workers were found to be without proper documentation and were attempting to return to Cambodia from Rayong and Chanthaburi. They are currently being processed at Ban Plaeng Police Station according to Thai law.
title: Thailand ‘seizes’ 10 Cambodian migrant workers

summary: Data from the General Department of Customs and Excise shows Thai imports to Cambodia dropped 49.3% in January 2026 compared to last year, totaling $151 million. This follows the Cambodian government's ban on specific Thai imports, including vegetables, fruits, and all types of fuel (gasoline, diesel, LPG, LNG, etc.), implemented after border tensions flared in July 2025.
title: Imports from Thailand to Cambodia decrease by nearly 50% in January 2026

summary: The Cambodian government reaffirmed its 'dual-track' strategy: defending sovereignty while seeking diplomatic solutions. Spokesman Pen Bona revealed that Cambodia has sent nearly 700 formal diplomatic notes in the last six months protesting Thai actions. The government is also prioritizing aid for displaced citizens, including clearing household debt and restoring utilities.
title: Cambodia Prioritises Peaceful Diplomacy and Territorial Integrity Amid Border Tensions

summary: In a patriotic address, PM Hun Manet acknowledged the physical and emotional scars left by recent border fighting, including destroyed homes and schools. He asserted that 'territory and people' remain the top priority. He called for a peaceful resolution based on international law and colonial-era maps, specifically mentioning the need for Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) mechanisms to ensure fairness.
title: Turning pain into strength: PM's message during Cambodia-Thai border conflict

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet addressed the nation, explaining that the Royal Government cannot publicly disclose every tactical or diplomatic step regarding the border dispute. He emphasized that the government is working 'diligently' and that results, such as the management of refugees and repairs to war-damaged areas, are already visible. He asked citizens for their 'trust and understanding' as the state navigates sensitive legal and military negotiations.
title: Hun Manet urges public understanding over border dispute measures with Thailand

summary: Bilateral trade has been severely impacted by the ongoing border tensions. Following the initial outbreak of conflict in July 2025, the Cambodian government banned the import of several Thai goods, including fuel, petroleum products, vegetables, and fruits. Statistics for January 2026 show a nearly 50% drop in imports from Thailand compared to the previous year, as Cambodia seeks to leverage economic pressure and source essential goods from other partners.
title: Cambodia–Thailand trade slumps as imports from Thailand plunge nearly 50% in January 2026

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet emphasized that safeguarding territorial integrity and citizens is the government's 'supreme priority.' He reaffirmed that the border is an international boundary protected by the UN Charter and stated Cambodia will not recognize any border alterations made through force. He insisted on a peaceful resolution through international law and existing colonial-era maps.
title: People and territory come first for Cambodia, PM says

summary: Despite a 87% return rate of displaced persons following the December 27 ceasefire, over 82,000 Cambodians remain in displacement camps. PM Hun Manet urged the nation to 'turn pain into strength,' acknowledging the emotional toll of the conflict while insisting that Cambodia will resolve the dispute through international law. Reports indicate that 14 schools and 7 health centers remain closed in Oddar Meanchey due to safety concerns and damage.
title: Hun Manet calls for unity as thousands remain displaced

summary: The Cambodian Mine Action Authority (CMAA) clarified its stance on anti-personnel mines near the border following Thai military allegations. Simultaneously, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a protest after reports that Thai forces destroyed civilian infrastructure and administrative buildings in the Boeng Trakuon area between border markers 33 and 34. In a separate emotional development, a Cambodian officer captured in December 2025 has finally returned home.
title: Cambodia responds to Thai reports of landmines, while noting destruction at Boeng Trakuon

summary: Keo Remy, Chairman of the Cambodian Human Rights Committee, met with Japanese Ambassador Ueno Atsushi. The Cambodian side accused Thailand of ongoing aggression and military occupation despite the Dec 2025 ceasefire. They reported that 90,000 displaced Cambodians still cannot return home because Thai troops are using shipping containers and barbed wire to block them. The ambassador reportedly promised to relay these concerns to the new Japanese government.
title: Keo Remy: Japanese Ambassador promises to relay border dispute issues to new Tokyo government

summary: The Cambodian Mine Action and Victim Assistance Authority (CMAA) rejected implications that Cambodia laid new mines after Thai forces reported finding an 'encroaching' Cambodian base and a MBV-78A2 landmine in Trat province. CMAA stated that Cambodia follows international treaties and any mines found are legacy devices from past conflicts, warning that unverified claims could increase unnecessary tensions.
title: Thai Military Finding of Border Anti-Personnel Mines Are Likely Legacy Device, Cambodia Asserts

summary: On February 11, the Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a strong protest against the Thai military for destroying civilian infrastructure and administrative buildings in the Boeung Trakuon area (between markers 33-36) and digging canals and building roads in Chouk Chey village (between markers 46-47). Cambodia views these as attempts to create 'facts on the ground' to legitimize illegal occupation.
title: Cambodia protests against Thai actions destroying administrative buildings at Boeung Trakuon and digging canals in Cambodian land

summary: Groups of Cambodian students and youth have expressed public outrage over what they describe as the continued Thai occupation of border provinces despite the ceasefire. Protesters are calling on the government to take faster action to reclaim territory and remove Thai blockades that prevent local villagers from accessing their homes and farms. The report captures rising nationalist sentiment among the younger generation following reports of Thai military infrastructure expansion.
title: Students denounce Thai blockade of Cambodian territory

summary: Dr. Kun Nhem, Director General of Customs and Excise, stated on February 12 that Cambodia has not faced shortages or high inflation despite the land border closure and a ban on strategic Thai imports like fuel, gasoline, and diesel. He noted that while imports from Thailand have plunged, customs revenue in 2025 actually increased by 21% due to internal efforts and diversification.
title: Closing border with Thailand has not caused Cambodia to lack goods or increase inflation

summary: General Romeo S. Brawner Jr., Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces of the Philippines, visited Cambodia to assess the border situation in Banteay Meanchey. Representing the ASEAN chair, he met with PM Hun Manet and confirmed the Philippines' readiness to lead the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) to facilitate a peaceful and impartial resolution to the ongoing dispute.
title: ASEAN chair Philippines monitoring Cambodia-Thailand border issue

summary: General Romeo S. Brawner Jr., Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces of the Philippines, met with PM Hun Manet on February 12 to confirm that the Philippines is ready to lead the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT), taking over from Malaysia. The team is tasked with verifying and monitoring the ceasefire along the border. Hun Manet updated the delegation on recent tensions and reiterated Cambodia's commitment to a peaceful resolution based on international law and the Franco-Siamese maps.
title: Philippines ready to lead AOT to resolve Cambodia-Thailand border issue

summary: Government spokesman Pen Bona accused Thai armed forces of 'unlawful activities' in Banteay Meanchey, including destroying civilian infrastructure near Boundary Pillars 33-36 and filling ponds to alter the terrain. Bona stated these actions are attempts to 'legitimize unlawful occupation' and reaffirmed that Cambodia will only accept borders defined by the 1904-1907 Franco-Siamese treaties.
title: Government Spokesman Says Cambodia Opposes Any Change to Borders by Force

summary: General Vong Pisen, Commander-in-Chief of the Royal Cambodian Armed Forces, met with Philippine counterpart Gen. Romeo S. Brawner Jr. in Phnom Penh. The Philippine general praised the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) and expressed a commitment to mediate the 'fragile' border dispute neutrally. He is scheduled to personally inspect the Banteay Meanchey border on February 13 to better understand the situation.
title: Philippine Military Chief Pledges Neutrality in Efforts to Resolve Cambodia-Thailand Border Dispute

summary: The Cambodian government, through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, has filed a strong protest against the Thai military for actions in Banteay Meanchey province. Reports from local authorities indicate Thai forces destroyed civilian infrastructure and government buildings in the Boeung Trakuon area (Pillars 33-36) and conducted unauthorized road and ditch construction in Chouk Chey village (Pillars 46-47).
